account.note: FOUR LEVELS CHECKED AGAINST LIVE QUOTES, FOUR CLEAR, NOTHING SOLD AND NO EXIT SPECIFICATION OWED. This slot's entire job is exits and this hour it had none to enforce. OKLO, 2 shares at a 45.1499 average against a 46.72 bid: +3.48%, 3.14 of unrealized gain on a 90.30 cost; the 54.18 target needs the bid up 15.97%, the 41.54 stop needs it down 11.09%, and the 8/14 close is the time stop with today session 2 of 5. NO OPTION IS HELD - the option position list was queried live and returned empty - so no no-fly window closes on anything. NO EARNINGS ON THE UNDERLYING: the calendar was re-pulled live at 760 events across 8/11 to 8/15 with OKLO in none of them, and SMCI on 8/11 pm, verified, 0.88 estimate, remains the only watched name inside the window. FIRED 14:21 AGAINST A 14:17 SLOT, four minutes late and well inside the guard, on quotes struck in a four-second window at 18:22:02-18:22:05 UTC so all twelve names are one timestamp. THE HOUR'S ONE REAL FINDING CUTS AGAINST WHAT THIS BOARD HAS BEEN SAYING, WHICH IS WHY IT LEADS. Three consecutive reads have described this universe as moving together, and the nuclear complex this hour does not: OKLO +5.01%, SMR +4.58%, LEU -2.24%. That is a 7.25-point spread inside one complex, widened from 6.62 points at 13:41, and it is the second consecutive read in which LEU has diverged from its two complex-mates. What that does and does not do to the two-per-complex cap, stated precisely because the temptation is to over-claim in either direction: it does NOT overturn the cap, because the cap rests on correlated stops gapping TOGETHER in a decline, which 8/10 demonstrated across twelve names and three separate stories, and dispersion on an up-move is not the case it guards. It does mean this board should stop describing co-movement as though it were uniform, because on this tape it is not, and where a quoted number and a written thesis disagree the number decides. THE POSITION IS THE BEST NAME ON THE LIST AND THAT CHANGES NOTHING. OKLO at +5.01% has passed SMR at +4.58% for the first time today, after eight consecutive reads on 8/10 as the worst name here. It is a rank; this slot acts on levels; the levels are clear. The stop at 11.09% away is the widest it has read since the fill, which is a fact about distance and not a licence to relax - it widened because the price rose, and it narrows the same way. BREADTH IMPROVED WITHOUT THE LEADERSHIP CHANGING: 6 green of 12 against 4 green, 1 flat and 7 red at 13:41, with AMD flipping green and RGTI off the flat print it held an hour ago. JOBY printed 8.33 bid at 13:41 and 8.33 bid now, identical to the cent across two reads - which this board has already learned means nothing, because SOUN printed 7.44 at four consecutive reads on Friday and it meant nothing then either. Recorded so it is not mistaken later for a floor. NO ENTRY, AND THE BAR WAS NOT CLOSE. The mid-session bar is higher than the open's by design; the daily entry mandate discharges through the open slot, which closed at the staleness guard 247 minutes late today and is not reopenable by this run; a one-session bounce in the names that fell hardest is a reversal off a decline rather than the day-2/3 pullback after strength the rulebook buys; the nuclear cap would permit exactly one of SMR or LEU beside this position; AMD at 470.42 is 46.4% of the account against a 40% single-name ceiling; and options remain refused on spread and were deliberately NOT re-quoted, because nothing is proposed and a quote pulled only to decorate a refusal is not evidence. ORDER RECORD QUERIED DIRECTLY A NINTH TIME AND UNCHANGED: exactly one order in this account since 8/7, the OKLO buy filled 10:39:30 ET on 8/10 at 45.1499 against a 45.40 limit, tagged agentic, with no specification from any run here behind it. The escalation stands open, unanswered and uncompounded. THE CONCURRENCY NOTE FROM 13:43 IS DROPPED FROM THE POSITION ROW RATHER THAN SILENTLY DELETED. It recorded that the 13:17 hourly and the open run wrote in the same minute on a 46.54 and a 46.53 bid - two reads seconds apart, not a disagreement about anything. Its purpose is served, its full text sits in the note directly below this one and in the published history, and carrying it a third session would be hoarding rather than record-keeping. Deployable is 919.58 settled with nothing pending and no pending deposits.
account.priorNote: THIS RUN STOPPED AT THE STALENESS GUARD AND PUBLISHED NOTHING. THE DAILY ENTRY MANDATE IS UNDISCHARGED FOR 2026-08-11. The open slot fired at 13:40 ET against an 09:33 ET slot: 247 minutes late, four hours and seven minutes, against a guard of 25 minutes in either direction. WHY THE MANDATE LOSES TO THE GUARD, WHICH IS THE ONE DECISION ON THIS RUN WORTH DEFENDING. The mandate says standing aside is not available to this slot, and the guard says a run this far outside its window publishes nothing. The guard wins by its own terms, and the reason is not procedural: an entry struck at 13:40 is not the open's entry carrying a late timestamp. It is a mid-session entry written by the one slot with a standing licence to open positions, on a tape four hours removed from the reasoning behind it, and it would enter the record labelled 'open' and corrupt the exact comparison the mandate was created to produce. A forced entry is a compromised thesis, honestly labelled. A stale entry is a compromised timestamp, and this board has no label for that. So 2026-08-11 has no specification and the run row carries the reason. FIVE SCHEDULED SLOTS PRODUCED NO ROW AT ALL BEFORE 13:40. The 09:33 open and the 10:17, 11:17, 12:17 and 13:17 hourlies each wrote nothing - not a decline, not a failed connection, no evidence they fired. That is the desktop-scheduler failure mode already described in the scheduler note, escalated rather than diagnosed from here, and it is a larger fact about today than anything on the tape. WHAT THE GUARD DID NOT COST IS AN EXIT, AND THAT IS A FACT ABOUT TODAY RATHER THAN A DEFENCE OF ARRIVING LATE. Exits were checked before anything else and all four levels on the one open position are clear: OKLO, 2 shares at a 45.1499 average against a live 46.53 bid, +3.06%, 2.76 of unrealized gain on a 90.30 cost, a 54.18 target that needs the bid up 16.44%, a 41.54 stop that needs it down 10.72%, and the 8/14 close as the time stop with today session two of five. An open position went from Friday's 16:33 retro to 13:40 today with no run looking at it. Had a level been through in that window it would have gone four hours unenforced, and nothing about this run's diligence would have changed that. NO OPTION IS HELD, so no no-fly window closes anything: the option position list was queried live and is empty, stated rather than assumed. NO EARNINGS ON THE UNDERLYING - the calendar was pulled live at 760 events across 8/11 to 8/15, OKLO in none of them, SMCI on 8/11 pm verified at an 0.88 estimate still the only watched name inside the window. No straddle was owed on the position and none is claimed. THE PRE-CLOSE NAMED A RISK THAT DID NOT ARRIVE, AND NOBODY GETS CREDIT FOR IT. Friday's close wrote down that OKLO had fallen 7.44% in a session and that another move of that size lands at 41.49, through the 41.54 stop, then held anyway on the rulebook's ground that a position closes at a level and not at a forecast. The session went the other way: 44.49 settled close to 46.53, +4.59%, and the stop is now 10.72% away, wider than at any read yesterday. Writing the danger down in advance was correct AND the direction it resolved in was forecast by nobody. Those are two separate findings, and the run that named the downside has no more claim on this outcome than one that had named the upside would have. BREADTH INVERTED AND THE LEADERSHIP INVERTED WITH IT: 4 green, 1 flat, 7 red against 10 red of 12 on Friday, and the two names leading today are the two that led the decline - SMR best at +4.90% and OKLO second at +4.59%, both nuclear, after finishing 8/10 fourth-worst and worst respectively. JOBY is the worst name on the board at -5.45% having closed Friday as the best. THE 8/10 OFFICIAL CLOSE IS NOW PUBLISHED AT 44.49, the regular-session figure the retro named as its alternative rather than the 44.20 extended-hours mark it used; the retro's own stated alternative total of 1008.56 is the one the settled data supports. Left for the bench and perf rows to correct rather than edited here. ORDER RECORD QUERIED DIRECTLY AND NOW CARRIED INTO A SECOND SESSION: exactly one order exists in this account since 8/7, the OKLO buy filled 10:39:30 ET on 8/10 at 45.1499 against a 45.40 limit, placed_agent agentic, with no specification from any run here behind it. The escalation stands open, unanswered and uncompounded. Deployable is 919.58 settled with nothing pending and no pending deposits. CONCURRENCY, RECORDED BECAUSE IT AFFECTED THIS FILE: the 13:17 hourly fired in the same minute as this run and wrote a position-only sync here at 13:43:52 on a 46.54 bid while this run held a 46.53 read struck at 17:41:23 UTC. Its note is preserved verbatim on the position below rather than overwritten; this board is struck at one timestamp across all twelve names; and the one-cent gap is two reads seconds apart rather than a disagreement about anything.
account.operatorNote: OPERATOR, 2026-08-10, answering the funding escalation carried in the notes above rather than editing either of them. The 900.00 is a deposit I made; the account is funded to about 1000 and the cash is spendable. This answers the deposit and NOTHING ELSE - it is not an authorisation for the OKLO order the 10:46 sync found, which no run here published and which arrived through the same agentic channel escalated on 8/7; that escalation stands open and unanswered. Three rule changes go with it and all three are written up in docs/RULES.md with their arithmetic, because a licence recorded without its constraints is how this record stops being worth reading. The position ceiling goes from two to four, capped at 40% in any one name and at two names in any one complex - the complex cap is the one that matters on a board whose whole universe moves together. Overnight holds are not a change: they were always allowed, the five-session time stop stands, and it is not extendable by conviction. The objective is still about 10% a day, which is roughly 101 dollars at this size and needs a fully deployed four-name book to average +10% in a session against a +20% take-profit; where the objective and the rulebook conflict, the rulebook wins and the retro records the shortfall. What the deposit does NOT do is reopen options - that refusal has been on spread for three sessions, most recently 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling, and no balance narrows a spread. The 10:22 hourly was right to escalate this rather than size against it.

entryWatch.setup: The open slot did not fire in its window - the entry mandate is unmet for 2026-08-11
entryWatch.trigger: None, and deliberately none. The staleness guard closed that slot at 13:40 ET, 247 minutes after 09:33. It is not reopenable later in the day by this run or any other: the mid-session slots are exits-only and the pre-close may not open a position in the last thirty minutes.
entryWatch.why: CARRIED FORWARD UNCHANGED BY THE SLOT THAT CANNOT DISCHARGE IT, WHICH IS THE POINT OF LEAVING IT ON THE BOARD. The mandate says standing aside is not available to the open slot; the guard says a run far outside its window publishes nothing; the guard won by its own terms this morning and the day therefore has no specification. This 14:21 hourly is explicitly NOT a second chance at it. The mid-session slot's job is exits and its bar for a new entry is higher than the open's by design - an entry written here at 14:21 would be a mid-session entry wearing the open's label, which is the same corruption of the record the guard refused at 13:40, arrived at by a different route. THE CAUSE IS UPSTREAM OF JUDGEMENT AND IS THE KNOWN ONE: the scheduler is a desktop task that fires only while the operator's app is open, and five slots today - the open and four hourlies - produced no row at all before 13:40. This run, at four minutes late, is the first of the day to fire in its own window. That is one data point, not a fix, and the escalation stands.

That pass belongs to the 15:33 pre-close, which is also the run that prunes this row once the print has passed.

entryWatch.setup: The speculative complex - a broadening bounce, and the first clear crack in the co-movement reading
entryWatch.trigger: No level. 6 green of 12 against 4 green, 1 flat and 7 red at 13:41, with the nuclear complex now spread 7.25 points between its best and worst names.
entryWatch.why: THE CO-MOVEMENT FINDING TOOK ITS FIRST REAL DAMAGE THIS HOUR, AND IT IS LED WITH RATHER THAN BURIED BECAUSE IT CUTS AGAINST WHAT THIS BOARD HAS SAID FOR THREE READS. Nuclear is not one trade today: OKLO +5.01%, SMR +4.58%, LEU -2.24%. That spread was 6.62 points at 13:41 and is 7.25 points now, so it widened rather than closed, and LEU has now sat out its complex for two consecutive reads. The honest reading is narrower than either extreme. The two-per-complex cap is NOT weakened: it was written about stops gapping together in a DECLINE, which 8/10 demonstrated across twelve names and three unrelated stories in a single hour, and a complex dispersing on an up-move is simply not the case the cap guards. What is weakened is the looser claim this board has been repeating - that these names move as one thing generally. On today's tape they do not, and the standing tiebreak says the number wins and the thesis is discarded rather than argued with. NOTHING IS PROPOSED, AND ON THIS RUN THAT IS THE SLOT RATHER THAN THE READ. The mandate discharges through the open slot and the open slot is closed; the row above carries that. Independently of it, this is also not the setup the rulebook buys - a second-session bounce in the names that fell hardest is a reversal off a decline, not the day-2/3 pullback after strength - and the complex cap would allow exactly one of SMR or LEU beside the OKLO position in any case. THE DEAD JOBY SPECIFICATION IS RE-MARKED A NINTH TIME AND SAYS NOTHING NEW, WHICH IS ITSELF THE ENTRY. The forced 8.85 limit expired unfilled at 10:30 on 8/10. JOBY is 8.33 bid, -5.88% against that limit and -5.45% on the day - the identical bid it printed at 13:41, to the cent. The eighth mark was worth a line because the gap had widened decisively; the ninth is worth a line only to record that an unchanged print is not a floor, on the same board where SOUN held 7.44 across four consecutive reads on Friday and it meant nothing.
